OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[-0-9 ().+]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when not supplied.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even if another owner already has the same last
            name and address (i.e. they share a household), assigning the joining owner and the
            existing household members a shared householdId. Otherwise such a request is rejected
            with 409 Conflict. Write-only control flag; the flag itself is not stored or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID

## Summary

I implemented the business-day rule for owner registration in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`:

1. **Effective date computation** — The effective registration date is taken from the request (`registrationDate`) when supplied, otherwise defaulted to `LocalDate.now()`. This single date is then rolled forward through a new `toBusinessDay(...)` helper: a **Saturday → next Monday** (+2 days), a **Sunday → next Monday** (+1 day), and a weekday is unchanged.

2. **Applied uniformly** — The adjusted date is always written via `owner.setRegistrationDate(registrationDate)`, replacing the old "default only when null" logic. This means a **supplied weekend date is now rolled forward too** (a behaviour change), not just the defaulted one.

3. **Derived values use the adjusted date** — Because the membership number (`OwnerMapper.toMembershipNumber`, whose `YY` segment reads `registrationDate.getYear()`) derives from the stored `registrationDate`, it automatically uses the adjusted date with no further change.

4. **Daily create-limit counts per adjusted business day** — `requireDailyLimitNotReached` now takes the adjusted `businessDay` and counts existing owners whose `registrationDate` equals it, and it's called *after* the date is adjusted, so the cap is enforced per business day.

The spec I was given only concerns Saturday/Sunday roll-forward (the active `AcceptanceTest` asserts the default registration date is never a weekend), so I intentionally did **not** implement holiday-skipping — even though the test base has an unused `toBusinessDay`/`HOLIDAYS` helper, the given specification and active test scope this to weekends only.

Result: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — **BUILD SUCCESS**.
